title: Stills

description.main: A 2016 book-and-vinyl collaboration between Belgian collage artist Katrien De Blauwer and American composer Danny Clay, issued as IIKKI 001, the debut release of the French label IIKKI. De Blauwer's 75 collages of found and recut photographs run alongside Clay's original composition, released as a matching LP.
description.extended:
Stills is a call-and-response between the Belgian collage artist Katrien De Blauwer and the American composer Danny Clay, issued in 2016 as IIKKI 001 — the debut release of the French label IIKKI, which pairs a visual artist with a musician for each of its book-and-vinyl editions.

Working independently over several months in 2016 from a shared set of prompts, De Blauwer and Clay never saw or heard each other's work in progress. Her 75 collages — spliced figures, torn interiors, sepia fragments recut from old magazines — and his piano, voice, harmonium, and viola composition (with Paula Karolak, mastered by Taylor Deupree) converge on a shared mood of memory and disappearance. The 112-page hardcover, designed by Sprflxgrfzm on Munken white stock with an embossed circle and slot, appeared in a first edition of 500 copies alongside a matching 500-copy LP, meant to be viewed and heard separately and together.

De Blauwer (b. 1969, Ronse, Belgium) calls herself a "photographer without a camera," building every image from cut and recombined found photographs. Stills was nominated for the Revelation Book Awards at La Maison Rouge, Paris, and stands among the clearest translations of her collage practice into collaborative, cross-media form.
description.artist_bio: Katrien De Blauwer (b. 1969, Ronse, Belgium) is a self-taught collage artist who calls herself "a photographer without a camera." Working exclusively from found and recycled images — magazine and newspaper photographs from the 1920s through the 1960s — she has made collage her sole medium since 1993, producing books and editions with publishers including Libraryman, Chose Commune, and Art Paper Editions, and exhibiting through galleries including Les Filles du Calvaire (Paris), Gallery Fifty One (Antwerp), and Rosegallery (Santa Monica).
